items.name: Paul Krugman
items.title: bubbel trubbel
items.position: Transcript of a Nov 12 conversation with Jared Bernstein and Jason Furman. The three largely agree AI is probably a bubble but not certainly; Krugman says he is 'surprisingly uncertain in my own judgment here'. The direct GDP hit from a bust would be small because data-center kit is mostly imported; the bigger channels are the wealth effect and financial conditions, with worry about opacity, private credit, off-balance-sheet vehicles and circular financing (Krugman raises the 2008 AIG analogy). A burst within two years would see little fiscal response given gridlock; he compares US fiscal/political risk to France.
items.sign_basis: Krugman and guests treat AI as a probable bubble with financial-fragility spillovers, though he flags his own uncertainty.

items.position: With the economy and markets so leveraged to AI, what happens to Nvidia's financial structure is systemically important: the 'central bank of AI' sits at the center of a web of interdependent funding (equity stakes, vendor financing, compute commitments, often with financially vulnerable firms), contract terms are not public so durability under stress is uncertain.
